model: MicroTech II AAF-HermanNelson Unit Ventilator Controller
applies_to: McQuay AAF-HermanNelson unit ventilators with the MicroTech II unit ventilator controller (software models 00-18) and the BACnet MS/TP communication module.
summary: The MicroTech II unit ventilator controller talks BACnet MS/TP through an optional communication module (LonWorks and N2 Open are the other options). The list has 54 objects: occupied/standby/unoccupied setpoints, damper and economizer settings, occupancy, mode and emergency commands, enables for economizer, compressor and auxiliary heat, sensor values the BAS can override, and status, run-time and fault values. Which objects apply depends on the unit's software model.
firmware: BACnet module firmware 3.00 and higher (state numbers)
notes: Object names are the names in the guide's full references (MTII UVUC ##########.<name>). Three are not usable as printed and keep the table's point name: MO 9 (its reference repeats MI 3's EffectOccup), AI 4 (repeats AI 5's SpaceCO2) and AV 12 (no reference printed).
Multistate state numbers are the firmware 3.00+ values (after 08/01/2003); firmware 2.08/2.09 used 0-based numbers with 255 = Null.
Table 16 of the guide marks which objects exist for each software model 00-18 (e.g. compressor objects only on heat pump/DX models, valve and F&BP damper objects only on hydronic models).
AI 1-5 and AI 18 accept writes only after Out_Of_Service is set TRUE; a valid written value overrides the local sensor.
AI 11 and AI 17 carry enumerated values (controller state and fault number) although they are analog inputs.
The device instance is set at the factory from the last four digits of the board serial number.
The table lists the source water temperature as AI 18; its detail page shows it as an Analog Output.

source.title: MicroTech II AAF-HermanNelson Unit Ventilator Unit Controller Protocol Information (BACnet, LonWorks, N2 Open)

integration.summary: Set the MS/TP MAC address on the module's S1 switch, give each controller a unique device instance, then schedule the unit with Occupancy Sensor Input (MO 9) and leave Application Mode on Auto. Write the occupied setpoints only when they change, and read occupancy, controller state, space temperature and the fault value.

minimum_points.name: ApplicMode
minimum_points.why: Unit mode; leave on Auto or Null normally

integration.enable: Occupancy Sensor Input (MO 9) is the object to use for BAS occupancy scheduling; the local bypass button overrides it for the Local Bypass Time (AV 7). Occupancy Override Input (MO 1) has the highest priority and overrides the sensor and tenant override. Application Mode (MO 2) should stay Auto or Null for normal operation.
integration.remote_sensors: Space temperature, outdoor temperature, outdoor and space humidity, space CO2 and entering water temperature (AI 1-5, AI 18) can be written by the BAS after setting Out_Of_Service TRUE; a valid value overrides the local sensor.
setup: MS/TP MAC address 0-127 is set with switches 1-7 of S1 on the communication module; switch 8 stays OFF (master).
Device instance comes from the last four digits of the board serial number; change it from the BAS if it clashes.
Device name is MTII UVUC plus the 10-digit board serial number.
Some software models need extra settings changed with MicroTech II Service Tools (Table 11 of the guide).
gotchas: All analog values are stored in EEPROM; don't write setpoints cyclically.
Use MO 9, not MO 1, for scheduled occupancy.
State numbers changed with module firmware 3.00 (August 2003); older modules use 0-based values.
